findings.statement: CXCR2 is the top convergence gene: pooled UC vs control log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.814], up in all eight cohorts, and in the paired inflamed vs non-inflamed contrast [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.6972]. Non-inflamed mucosa shows only a small rise [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.6399], so it marks local inflammation. CXCR2 is mainly a neutrophil receptor, so the bulk signal probably reflects neutrophil infiltration; antagonists (navarixin, reparixin, ladarixin) are in phase 2 and phase 3 trials.

CXCL8 (IL-8), the CXCR1 and CXCR2 ligand, is strongly and reproducibly up: pooled log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.864] with the same direction in all eight cohorts. The change holds after adjustment for colon segment, age and sex in MSCCR [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_adjusted; source=DATASET:GSE193677; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed UC vs control, biopsy level; adjusted_log2fc=2.499]. It is a local inflammation marker, with a large myeloid and neutrophil contribution.

HMGCS2, an epithelial ketogenesis and metabolism gene, is strongly down in all eight cohorts: pooled [gene=HMGCS2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.838]. It is unchanged in non-inflamed mucosa [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.0649], so the loss is local to inflamed tissue. Protein is also lost in an independent proteomics study [gene=HMGCS2; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=-3.094]. The change survives covariate adjustment. It is a biomarker of epithelial metabolic collapse, not a target.

CHI3L1 is among the largest and most reproducible increases: pooled [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.875], up in all eight cohorts and in paired inflamed mucosa, and robust to covariate adjustment. The protein rise is much smaller [gene=CHI3L1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.607] and the proteomics authors did not call it significant, although the BH padj is small; RNA is far stronger than protein. No drug is known.

IDO1 is up in all eight cohorts, pooled [gene=IDO1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.118], and the independent proteomics replicates it at protein level [gene=IDO1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.917]. It is an interferon-driven inflammation gene, with a stronger paired change in inflamed mucosa. Clinical IDO1 inhibitors exist but come from oncology; there is no genetic support.

JAK2 has strong genetic association in Open Targets and a highly significant but modest pooled increase [gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.874], up in all eight cohorts. It is a small shift in a broadly expressed signalling kinase, so its rank rests on genetics and tractability rather than on expression size; the JAK pathway acts through activity rather than mRNA abundance.

MMP3 is one of the strongest increases, pooled [gene=MMP3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.901], up in all eight cohorts and in paired inflamed mucosa. It is a stromal and mucosal-damage marker. MMP1, MMP7 and MMP10 follow the same pattern. Broad MMP inhibitors (marimastat) have failed historically, so this is a tissue-injury biomarker more than a target.

DUOX2, an epithelial reactive-oxygen gene (with DUOXA2 also in the top increases), is up in all eight cohorts: pooled [gene=DUOX2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.412]. The change is large in paired inflamed mucosa and comes from epithelium, so it is not only infiltrating cells. It is a strong biomarker of epithelial inflammatory stress; it has no genetic support or drugs in the ranking.

S100A8 (with S100A9 and S100A12, calprotectin components) is up in all eight cohorts: pooled [gene=S100A8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.77]. The signal is largely neutrophil and monocyte derived, so the increase tracks infiltration rather than a change inside the tissue; the cell-context analysis should check this. Its value is as a faecal and tissue activity biomarker, not as a target.

CD274 (PD-L1) is up in all eight cohorts, pooled [gene=CD274; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=1.974], with genetic support in Open Targets. It most likely reflects interferon-driven induction in inflamed mucosa and immune cell influx, so it indicates an immune-regulation feedback pathway rather than a drug target to inhibit (checkpoint blockade carries colitis risk).

SLC26A3 (the chloride/bicarbonate exchanger, a UC genetic locus) is down in all eight cohorts, pooled [gene=SLC26A3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-1.702]. It combines genetic support with loss of epithelial absorptive function, and the paired inflamed vs non-inflamed contrast is also negative. It is a restoration-biology candidate, not an inhibitable target.

AQP8 shows the largest pooled decrease among the downregulated genes [gene=AQP8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-5.246], significantly down in most cohorts. Together with CLDN8, PCK1 and GUCA2A/B it forms a colonocyte differentiation and absorption signature lost in inflamed mucosa, which makes a good activity biomarker panel.

caveats: Pooled heterogeneity is very high for nearly all top genes (I2 above 0.9), driven by platform differences and compressed microarray fold changes; direction is consistent but size is not.

Bulk biopsies: increases in neutrophil, myeloid and lymphoid genes (CXCR2, CXCL8, S100A8, IL1B, CD274) may reflect infiltrating cells rather than tissue-intrinsic change; the cell-context specialist must confirm.
Proteomics is available only for a subset of genes, and a gene not measured is not evidence against it.
Adjusted-change and paired analyses were run only in MSCCR and only on selected genes; not all findings were individually checked for non-inflamed mucosa.
